newsitem.title: UK: Thermo Electron unit buying British instrument firm.
newsitem.headline: Thermo Electron unit buying British instrument firm.

text.p: Thermo Instrument Systems Inc. offered 236 million pounds ($392 million) cash Tuesday to acquire Life Sciences International Plc, a British producer of scientific equipment.

The offer of 135 pence ($2.24) a share from Thermo, a subsidiary of Thermo Electron Corp. of Waltham, Mass., follows its purchase last year of Fisons Plc's worldwide scientific instruments division for 202 million pounds ($335 million).

Thermo said Life Sciences' manufacturing, distribution and service base will help it extend its product offerings into new markets, such as clinical laboratory equipment, and will enhance its presence in the bio-analytical instrumentation marketplace.
Thermo develops and manufactures instruments used to detect and measure air pollution, radioactivity, complex chemical compounds, toxic metals and other elements.
It said the acquisition will be financed from its cash resources and expects the purchase to enhance earnings immediately.
The company also revealed that it will continue to keep an eye on possible further acquisitions.

"We are in discussion with a number of companies all the time, some in Europe, some in the U.S, some in the Far East," Earl Lewis, executive vice president and chief operating officer of Thermo Instruments, said in an interview.
"At any point in time there are anywhere up to 30 or 40 companies that we are actively watching."
Thermo Electron's stock added 12.5 cents to $36.75 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
